issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
### What

Evaluate ScienceAgentBench Verified for inclusion in Marin’s in-distribution (ID) evaluation policy. The solver uses Pi to write a Python program against supplied scientific data. EvalDash replays the submitted program in a clean environment and grades its output. Verified revises the original 102-task release and retains its task IDs. Our panel covers 101 tasks. Task 78 is recorded as unrun in both conditions. [Verified release](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench#updates) · [Implementation PR #11599](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11599)

The annotation pin is `9c6e96c9`. At that revision, 41 of 102 rows differ from the original annotations, including nine task instructions. The existing Harbor adapter reads the legacy split without pinning the Hugging Face revision. The Marin implementation uses pinned software environments and stages each task’s checksummed data after startup. [Pinned annotations](https://huggingface.co/datasets/osunlp/ScienceAgentBench/tree/9c6e96c9e74572e979b0930ee735041cef528cb7) · [Harbor adapter](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/pull/630)

Run the same tasks twice per model, once with the authors’ expert knowledge in the prompt and once without it. Report the fraction of tasks passed separately for each condition. Of the 101 eligible tasks, 37 use programmatic checks and 64 require figure comparisons. For the figure tasks, the current panel uses Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct via Venice on OpenRouter. The publisher used GPT-4o-2024-05-13. We send three independent requests per figure, average the scores, and apply the published task threshold. A completed reply missing the score marker contributes zero. A failed request leaves the trial ungraded. [Paper and author protocol](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05080v3)

The merged agent evaluation runtime records Pi as the operation of the curated corpus. ScienceAgentBench uses a native importer for the Verified release. Marin’s add-eval skill directs live agent episodes to this TaskSpec and RolloutEngine route. The implementation PR now includes the upstream merge; the production recipes use the same Pi installation helper as BixBench with Pi pinned to 0.87.0. New corpus builds have revision `2026.11.24.2`. The Qwen runs below retain their earlier pinned corpus and solver identities. [Merged runtime PR #11664](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11664) · [Agent evaluation reference](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d732910d5e9375be66132e37a083f7be6722e380/docs/references/evaluation-tasks.md) · [Updated add-eval skill](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d732910d5e9375be66132e37a083f7be6722e380/.agents/skills/add-eval/SKILL.md)

### Why

The policy question is whether Marin can use this benchmark to track how well cohort models turn a scientific instruction and a dataset into a correct result. The tasks span bioinformatics, computational chemistry, geographical information science, and psychology and cognitive science. Clean replay lets us check the artifact the program actually produces. The paired prompts let us measure how much the same solver benefits from domain guidance, a distinction the authors also studied. [Marin evaluation policy #10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197) · [Paper, Table 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05080v3#S4.T3)

### Validation

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, completed November 24. Without expert knowledge Qwen passed **17/101 (16.8%)**. The two original EvalDash archives supply 99 grades. For the last two tasks, a CPU verifier replayed the saved Qwen programs, verified their identities by SHA-256, and used the pinned plot rubric, threshold, and Venice judge. Tasks 76 and 84 each scored zero with three judge receipts. The original knowledge-off plot run is marked failed in EvalDash. The 101-task aggregate includes the two supplemental records. With expert knowledge Qwen passed **28/101 (27.7%)**. [Knowledge-on EvalDash run](https://evaldash.oa.dev/runs/pipeline-qwen3.6-35b-a3b-scienceagentbench-verified-visual-knowledge-on-602ccee4aac95e35aaedba898a054351) [Deterministic results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11592#issuecomment-7083615825) · [Saved-program verification](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fexedev%2Fsab-qwen-saved-off-1124)

| Expert knowledge | Programmatic passes / graded | Plot passes / graded | Grading coverage | Overall pass rate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Off | 9/37 | 8/64 | 101/101 | 16.8% |
| On | 11/37 | 17/64 | 101/101 | 27.7% |

On the same 101 tasks, 11 passed in both conditions, 17 passed only with expert knowledge, and 6 passed only without it. The observed difference was +10.9 percentage points.

| Sensitivity analysis | Knowledge off | Knowledge on |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Exclude task 41 | 17/100 | 28/100 |
| Exclude four flagged references (41, 59, 96, 102) | 17/97 | 27/97 |
| Exclude exposed answers (53, 58) | 16/99 | 27/99 |

- **Grader checks.** On four recovered Qwen outputs, the publisher’s deterministic scorer and the EvalDash adapter agreed on one pass and three failures. Both also passed the reference output for each of the three distinct tasks. On eight selected Qwen submissions, the substitute plot judge and the authors’ GPT-4o snapshot agreed on 6/8 pass/fail decisions using identical replayed PNGs. [Plot-judge comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11592#issuecomment-7140588075). In a separate draw of 24 distinct tasks, the judges agreed on 19/22 comparable task verdicts. [Expanded comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11592#issuecomment-7141439329) Earlier MiniMax pilot grades and the 54 grades from the previous Pi revision are tracked separately. [Same-output grader comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11592#issuecomment-7111004800)
- **Publisher controls.** Across 101 eligible tasks, 29 deterministic references and 58 visual references passed in the reference campaign, four fell below threshold (41, 59, 96, 102), and ten lacked a completed comparison. Task 97 used an extended diagnostic replay allowance. The visual reference campaign predates the current Venice judge route. Report the headline score alongside sensitivity analyses omitting task 41, all four threshold failures, and the two tasks with exposed answers (53 and 58). Keep the released inputs and thresholds for headline results. [Reference evidence](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11592#issuecomment-7045716068)
- **Policy decision.** The paired Qwen evidence is complete across 101 eligible task IDs. Broader cohort comparisons and panel-wide visual-judge agreement remain open. The paper used different agents and reported best-of-three results. Its published scores are a historical comparison.

### Cost

Each completed model panel covers 202 trials. The configuration allows 60 minutes for solving and 30 minutes for verification, including up to 15 minutes for clean replay. Each sandbox requests 2 CPUs, 8 GiB RAM and 10 GiB disk. The two Qwen plot archives and the supplemental verifier ledger show 354 settled calls (USD 0.5433) and 18 outstanding call reservations (up to USD 0.5220). These figures cover the paired Qwen plot panel. Accelerator-hours and the provider invoice have not been reconciled.

issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
Serving `IFM/K2-Horizon-375B-A23B` in BF16 across two nodes fails at startup. Its config class comes from the repository's remote code, and the headless executor on the second node cannot pickle that class when it spawns its workers:

```
File ".../vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 748, in make_worker_process
...
File ".../multiprocessing/reduction.py", line 60, in dump
_pickle.PicklingError: Can't pickle <class 'transformers_modules.e7a74a2f.2e613447f4c0369a.configuration_k2_horizon.K2HorizonConfig'>: it's not the same object as transformers_modules.e7a74a2f.2e613447f4c0369a.configuration_k2_horizon.K2HorizonConfig
RuntimeError: HeadlessMultiprocExecutor_DP0 exited unexpectedly with code None
```

This blocks K2 Horizon in BF16 as a comparison model for the Nov 30 eval policy. The 758 GB of BF16 weights exceed one 4x GB200 node (744 GB) and one 8x H100 node (640 GB), so it needs two pipeline stages. `--trust-remote-code` cannot be dropped: neither `transformers` 5.12 nor vLLM (Marin's fork at `47a8e415`, upstream v0.34.0, upstream main) ships a K2 Horizon config class. vLLM's `maybe_register_config_serialize_by_value` (`vllm/transformers_utils/config.py`) registers remote-code configs for by-value pickling, but the headless multi-node path still pickles this class by reference.

Reproduce:
1. Write a model config for revision `7a17b47a74b9371e71ed64b4080192e01caa6174` with `resource_hint.gpu: {GB200: 4}`, `memory: 768g`, `tensor_parallel_size: 4`, `pipeline_parallel_size: 2`, and `vllm_extra_args: [--enable-prefix-caching, --enable-expert-parallel, --trust-remote-code, --chat-template-content-format, string]` on the default GPU vLLM release (`marin-vllm-gpu-20261118-47a8e415bff1`).
2. Run `uv run python -m experiments.evaluation.cli launch --model-config <file> --evals smoke --limit 20 --priority interactive`.
3. The second stage's task fails about two minutes after vLLM starts. Iris job: `/chrismcconnell/eval-20261124-165606-k2-horizon-375b-a23b-b9e5c4d22cbf4bcc8cd3e08c6d09013a-8ed94485`.

Expected: both pipeline stages start and the endpoint serves requests.

Part of #12156. cc @yonromai @rjpower

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

On the headless node, vLLM loads K2 Horizon's remote config and registers a multiprocessing reducer for `VllmConfig`. It then spawns a headless executor, which spawns the GPU workers. The reducer is registered per process; the reported class-identity `PicklingError` at the second spawn is consistent with the executor process lacking it. A nested-spawn test is needed to confirm that mechanism.

**Relevant code**
- [Marin headless launch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/142a4206575fc8b9be72d5b6cda833c2529165b8/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris_vllm.py#L244-L267) — adds `--headless` on follower nodes.
- [vLLM config loading](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/47a8e415bff17b9376f02d9b92edcc67e962eaee/vllm/transformers_utils/config.py#L884-L887) and [reducer](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/47a8e415bff17b9376f02d9b92edcc67e962eaee/vllm/transformers_utils/config.py#L1049-L1125) — registration happens during config loading.
- [Headless executor launch](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/47a8e415bff17b9376f02d9b92edcc67e962eaee/vllm/entrypoints/cli/serve.py#L191-L249) — first process spawn.
- [Worker launch](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/47a8e415bff17b9376f02d9b92edcc67e962eaee/vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py#L185-L205) and [process start](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/47a8e415bff17b9376f02d9b92edcc67e962eaee/vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py#L704-L749) — second process spawn.
- [Marin GPU release pin](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/142a4206575fc8b9be72d5b6cda833c2529165b8/config/external/vllm/gpu.toml#L1-L16) — currently uses `47a8e415`.

# Proposed Fix

1. In `marin-community/vllm`, add a test using a local remote-code config and two spawn generations. Confirm it fails with the reported `PicklingError` on `47a8e415`.
2. Register the `VllmConfig` reducer inside the headless executor process before it starts workers. Run the regression test and the existing standard-config multiprocessing tests.
3. Build a GPU release from the fixed fork. Update Marin's `gpu.toml` and `external_dependencies.py` pins with the release and wheel hashes.
4. Run the issue's two-node K2 Horizon smoke test with PP=2 and TP=4. Require both stages to become ready and complete requests before opening the Marin pin PR with `Fixes #12215`.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
Deploying the marin Iris hub controller needs a specific set of GCP permissions, but no role names that set. Operators get it ad hoc, and a new operator finds out what is missing only when a deploy fails partway.

On November 20 a controller rollout built and pushed images, then failed at two steps:

- writing the controller VM's startup metadata (`compute.instances.setMetadata` denied);
- SSH as the `iris-controller` service account (`iam.serviceAccounts.actAs` on the VM's default Compute service account denied).

The existing operators can deploy only because they hold broad roles such as `roles/editor` or `roles/owner`. PR 11875 fixed this for one operator by copying four deploy-relevant grants:

- `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1`
- `roles/compute.osAdminLogin`
- `roles/iap.tunnelResourceAccessor`
- `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` on the default Compute service account

Define one `marin-infra` grant set (custom role ID `marinInfra`) in `infra/pulumi/src/iac/gcp/iam_data.yaml` (a custom role, or one documented group of bindings), and grant operators that set instead of individual roles. Include the permissions the rollout needs end to end: image push, Token Creator on `iris-controller`, metadata write, SSH and IAP. Prefer the narrowest permissions that work, and test them with a real rollout.

Done when:

- `iam_data.yaml` has the `marinInfra` role, and the current operators hold it;
- the controller rollout reference and `lib/iris/OPS.md` name that role as the deploy prerequisite;
- an operator who holds only that role and `marindev` completes a checkpointed controller rollout.

comments.body:

## Research

[PR #11875](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11875) added separate deploy grants for one operator. Current `main` has no `marinInfra` role. ## Proposed Fix

1. Inventory the current controller operators by encrypted principal ID and their effective grants. Define `marinInfra` in `iam_data.yaml` with the smallest [testable custom-role permissions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/creating-custom-roles) for VM metadata, OS Login, and IAP tunnel access. Bind VM permissions to the hub instances where IAM conditions support that scope. 4. After IAM review and an explicitly scoped rollout authorization, test on `marin-dev` with an operator lacking `editor`, `owner`, and broad Compute roles. Run plan, preflight, baseline snapshot, checkpointed controller restart, smoke job, and the full five-minute verify. Record effective grants and any denied permission, then tighten the grant set before calling the issue done.

issues.author: znichols
issues.body:
## Goal

Produce the **first 10,000 accepted science RL tasks**, starting with computational-biology environments built from independently sourced, openly licensed data of the kind that supports BixBench-like analysis. This issue tracks **our task production**, not RL Atlas development; submit a task to RL Atlas only after it is rights-cleared and validated. Aim for distinct, executable analysis programs across genuinely independent source families—not paraphrases, changed thresholds, multiple model seeds, or benchmark questions.

A **bucket** is one source document or a coherent group of source documents/data files for a study. Record the bucket's source family, pinned manifest, rights and privacy evidence, the exact input projection, candidate analysis programs, TaskForge IDs, validation outcomes, and Atlas submission. A downloaded record is not automatically an independent bucket or a usable environment.

## Pipeline and counting rules

1. **Identified:** Find a plausible source bucket or family. Record study relationships, declared licenses, sensitivity flags and a file inventory. A search hit is not a cleared bucket.
2. **Archived:** Pin and checksum source bytes, selection and manifest immutably. Archive bytes are *never* automatically generator or solver inputs.
3. **Test extracted:** Run a small, bounded task-extraction/analysis pilot from source-only context; verify the relevant fields, units, joins and candidate computations. Three real-data buckets have one independently executed provisional analysis each. A schema/header probe alone does not count.
4. **Fully extracted:** Complete **all task extraction planned for that bucket under a stated, bounded extraction plan**, including attempts, explicit no-task/failed outcomes and a frozen candidate/disposition ledger. A completed *wave* says nothing about whether more task families could ever be mined; a new expanded plan needs its own version. **This phase is about task extraction, not licensing or solver-input projection.**
5. **TaskForged:** Turn the extracted candidate tasks into actual TaskForge TaskSpecs with deterministic graders, full keyset/answer contracts and negative controls. A model-produced idea or grader plan does not count. This label means *built*, not accepted for RL.
6. **Characterized:** Run fresh-agent solver trials, grader adversaries (including missing/extra/duplicate keys and plausible wrong methods), independent scientific/reference checks and private published-result/eval overlap review. Record difficulty, failures, Stage 50 evidence and a Stage 60 decision. Characterization may quarantine or reject a task.
7. **Landed:** Submit only rights-cleared, Stage 60-accepted tasks to RL Atlas with provenance, hashes, source-family split and validation evidence. Count toward 10k only here; no benchmark item text, keys, solved notebooks, teacher rollouts or private audits enter generation.

## Inventory: source collections versus individual buckets (2026-11-23)

I previously labeled **acquisition waves** as “buckets”; that was wrong. GTN and Zenodo search rounds are *ways we found material*, not three or four coherent source studies. We have a few **source collections** and **three individually test-extracted real-data buckets**; the 386 deposits still need study-family consolidation. A conditional planning estimate is not a count of tasks.

**Count units matter:** a page, repository, deposit, analysis idea and TaskSpec are different units. The cells below count progress within each *collection*, not individual independent studies. **Fully extracted means the documented, bounded task-extraction plan was finished, not that every conceivable task was found.** Constituent rights/privacy and a minimal hashed solver-input projection are **separate mandatory gates** before exposing real data to a new author/solver or landing tasks; campaign completion does not settle them. The older campaigns ran bounded waves without those gates being fully resolved.

| GTN + independently discovered Zenodo biology data | **1,156 record IDs** in deduplicated metadata library (*not* study families) | **386 distinct deposits**, 1,924 checksum-verified files | **3 individual source buckets** with verified source-only profiles and independently executed provisional analyses; further header-only probes do not count | **0 buckets** with completed extraction plans | **0** | **0** | **0** | **386–1,158** *hypothetical* analysis slots under an untested 1–3 per independent eligible record assumption; 0 verified tasks |

**Actual provisional TaskForge builds: 352 + 630 = 982 distinct ideas** (the combined BioTasks 305 are a *subset* of 352, not an extra cohort); **0 landed tasks**. Of the 982, the curated combined BioTasks snapshot has 305, so **935 = 305 + 630** is the narrower selected-snapshot count. Neither 982 nor 935 is training-cleared. The real-data archive adds **zero TaskForge builds** and only a non-forecast planning range. **770 of 1,156** Zenodo/GTN metadata IDs remain unacquired: **646** small leads in active/manual-review queues plus **124** separately held GTN records. No double-counting across acquisition rounds.

### Individual real-data bucket phase grid

`✓` complete, `·` not complete. Test extraction is a limited source-only task pilot; fully extracted means the bucket's **declared full task-extraction plan is complete**. None of these three has such a plan completed. Rights/privacy and solver projection are separate gates, not phases in this grid. These three are **within** the 386 acquired records.

### Acquisition pools (not buckets)

Counts below are **records or leads, not accepted buckets**. The downloaded-only planning range assumes *one to three different executable analyses per independently eligible source*, **before** rights, semantic deduplication, projection, grader and solver losses. It is a conditional workload ceiling/range, not a measured forecast; actual accepted yield from these sources is **zero**. The three pilot records are included in the 386 and must not be added again.

Downloaded bytes are verified but not cleared. | Downloaded: **121–363 hypothetical slots; 0 accepted**. **Combined acquired inventory:** **386 distinct records**, **1,924 verified files**, **2,593,708,509 bytes (~2.59 GB)**, with **386–1,158 conditional analysis slots** under the untested one-to-three assumption. A manifest hash/normalized-title audit does not prove independent study families. Four records contain nested archives. **Unacquired small leads:** 176 + 236 + 234 = **646**, with unknown yield. None of these cohorts is a 1,000–2,000 credible *usable-task* pool yet. Even if every qualifying source supplied three accepted tasks, 10k would require at least **3,334 independent usable families**; scale source discovery and validated program diversity rather than multiplying shallow variants.

**Existing-campaign caveat:** BioTasks' selected 305 have reference disputes and rights/release gates; its other 47 notebook TaskSpecs were excluded from that selected set. MedlinePlus/NHGRI's 630 passed structural preflight but page-rights and biology review remain, and three had only diagnostic solver/control trials. None is training-cleared. Benchmark archives and the 20-capsule profiling pilot's **96 unverified seeds** are **not source buckets**; original eval tasks, solutions and notebooks never enter generation.

**Per-bucket ledger to maintain from here:** `bucket_id | source_family_id | pinned_source_manifest | identified_at | archived_at | test_extracted_at | extraction_plan_id + planned distinct programs + stop rule | fully_extracted_at + candidate/no-task dispositions | taskforged_at | characterized_at + verdict | landed_at + Atlas IDs | separate constituent-rights/privacy verdict | solver_projection_sha256 | conditional/actual task yield | next blocker`. Merge deposits from one study under a single family; a disposition or `0` is a valid outcome. Keep audit-only identities and restricted details in the private ledger, not the public issue or generator context.

## Immediate milestones

- [ ] For the **three executable pilot analyses**, settle constituent-file rights/privacy and publish private, hash-pinned *allowlisted* solver projections (archive and private references remain inaccessible to solver/author).
- [ ] Implement TaskForge proposal sources and deterministic full-key graders for those three; test adversarial missing/extra/duplicate keys, numerical boundaries, malformed answers and plausible wrong methods.
- [ ] Run fresh-agent solver trials, independent biology and published-result checks, and private eval-overlap review. Record Stage 50/60 evidence or quarantine each task.
- [ ] Review more *independent* interaction, trait and OTU source families to measure eligible-source and accepted-analysis yield; keep per-bucket counts for distinct programs versus parameter variants.
- [ ] Triage the 386 acquisitions and 646 pending leads into a per-bucket ledger with explicit source-family merges and rights/hold decisions; expand source discovery until a credible 1,000–2,000 potential-task pool exists.
- [ ] Only after that pool gate, run a **separately authorized**, small, budget-capped input-generation/TaskForge pilot and measure cost per *accepted* candidate. Explicitly accounted-for pilots (including the 20-bundle experiment) cost $1.3856368, **not** a certified account total. The working GLM route (2026-11-23) removes an endpoint blocker, not source/validation gates. The user's planning target is about **$100 for ~1,000 candidates**, with the previous **$10 hard ceiling for three-record prompt experimentation**; neither authorizes a full wave.
- [ ] Define and verify the RL Atlas handoff contract, then submit only Stage 60-accepted, rights-cleared tasks; update this issue with submitted counts and evidence.

comments.body:
### Correction to the nine-call report: iterative source extraction is now underway

The initial **nine calls were prompt calibration**, not extraction to exhaustion; treating them as a finished source pilot was my mistake. I subsequently froze a **bounded four-round-per-(record, arm) extraction plan** for the same three allowlisted records and three approaches. Each round requested up to two distinct programs, with the actual selected source rows visible and read-only access to *all selected file rows* via a bounded `read_rows` tool and in-memory source-only SQL. No eval items, published solutions, unselected files or previous private answers were exposed. Own-arm prior questions, not other arms' outputs, are used to discourage repeats. Request/tool/result snapshots are versioned, with failed attempts retained rather than overwritten.

**Attempt accounting:** 3 records × 3 arms × 4 planned rounds = **36 attempted round cells** in addition to the nine calibration calls. A first runner mistakenly allowed the last tool turn to remain open; I cancelled it after 30 unfinished cells, preserved their paid traces and finalized those *without replaying the four already-made turns*. Six fourth-round cells were separately attempted: **33/36** yielded final candidate/no-task responses, while **3/36** reached a hard tool/finalization budget with no final task and retain that failure disposition. Among the 33 final responses, one explicitly said no-task and the rest yielded **63 raw proposals**: 24 interaction, 22 trait and 17 OTU; by arm: 20 objective-first, 22 question-first and 21 answer-first. These are neither 63 independent programs nor 63 reference-verified tasks. Every proposal's model-authored SQL executed successfully against the first source projection; that alone does **not** validate its question, method or answer.

A follow-on source-byte audit caught a **major projection error**, now immutably recorded: the trait CSV uses literal `NA`. The first SQLite tool retained it as text; aggregate functions treated it as zero rather than missing. The source has 44 `NA` for `lma`, 8 for `lwr`, 54 for `leaf_succulence` (other environmental fields also have missing values). Replaying only the already-frozen queries over a corrected NULL projection changes query results for **19/22 trait proposals**; their answers are **quarantined**, not silently patched. The correction snapshot is `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin4sc/taskforge/source-corpora/open-biology/source-content-three-arm-trait-na-correction-20261123-v1/summary.json` (SHA-256 `c2faab6b94a1bbf095ce5513aadac8d572ac8f4bff5af98e817c98e28c117e12`). Some interaction answers also contradict their own source-derived counts. The private 36-cell ledger is `.../source-content-three-arm-multiround-review-20261123-v2/summary.json` (SHA-256 `cc4439886d3c9b18834a6859d11618e2673319a55cfbfe848c02bb7f90aaa932`).

**Do not mark any of these buckets fully extracted yet.** Four rounds is a bounded *pass*, not proof of absolute exhaustion. The next gate is a per-proposal scientific/source-rights review, corrected independent reference computations, and analysis-program deduplication. Only then measure marginal **distinct, independently executable** yield by arm and decide whether to extend the plan or stop after recorded no-new-program rounds. Zero new TaskForge, training-cleared or landed tasks.

🤖 **Recipe ledger v1 — compare candidate production without mixing units**

A recipe is `(source cohort and input projection, output kind, prompt revision, model + decoding policy, source-access method, iteration/feedback rule, reference/selection policy)`. The first three are important, but changing the input or the kind of task also changes the experiment. A deposit, an independent study, a generator response, a proposal, a distinct analysis program and a TaskSpec are separate units.

**Output kinds:** (1) *source-native*: solve an analysis of immutable original input data; (2) *adapted*: make a small, frozen, honestly labeled input projection or transformation of permissible source data; (3) *synthetic analogue*: use source text/code as motivation but generate new self-contained data. All three can be useful. Track them in separate yield columns. Never let a solver see published answers, benchmark items, original solutions or private references.

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Plant–insect interactions `5600907` | 1 | 3 | 2 synthetic | 1 adapted + 1 synthetic | 0 |
| Plant traits `4942915` | 1 | 2 | 0 | 2 synthetic | 1 adapted (literal `\\n` inside CSV, no row breaks) |
| Insect OTUs `4971364` | 0 (explicit no-task) | 3 | 2 synthetic | 0 | 1 synthetic (malformed metadata header) |
| **Total** | **2** | **8** | **4 / 10** | **4 / 10** | **2 / 10** |

Independent Python/pandas references were computed only from the proposed frozen solver resources; **no model-generated code was executed**. The review compared the interaction adapted packet against source bytes: its aggregate rows match, but its claimed correlation and OLS answer does not; its `source_query` uses an unregistered table name. The trait packet's literal escaped newlines make its single CSV unreadable, so source lineage could not be checked. Four numeric matches are **not four high-quality tasks**: some synthetic problems are small pairwise calculations, and the NODF label/formula, study semantics, rights and novelty still need review. The numbers are one small trial and do not rank the two output kinds generally. Frozen private reference/source-lineage review: `.../zenodo-biotasks-like-six-20261124-review-v1/private_review.json` (SHA-256 `ad59ad3d736cf0c9bfc412ec7c6f88431fef80cd8f2326595575cc19a5859029`). **Zero TaskSpecs, rights-cleared tasks or landed tasks** result from this trial.

### Combined recipe to test next (hypothesis, not demonstrated high-yield pipeline)

1. **Discover distinct analysis programs against actual allowlisted inputs.** The model chooses a scientific objective, unit, required fields, reproducible operations and output contract using read-only file tools. It proposes multiple different programs per bucket and sees only its own prior program summaries. Keep the three prompt modes as experimental arms on matched inputs. De-duplicate across modes and rounds by source family + operation, not by prompt wording or changed parameter values.
2. **Choose an output kind per surviving program:** original-data solver input, a *deterministically materialized* small adapted projection with source-row lineage, or an explicitly synthetic analogue. Preserve these as distinct yield categories. The program can yield both an original-data task and a synthetic teaching task if they have genuinely distinct input/skill contracts; do not count a changed numeric instance twice. The generator must not freely type a source-derived CSV: it selects a validated projection, and code emits the resource bytes. For synthetic rows, accept typed fields/rows and have code serialize the files; reject malformed CSV before a build.
3. **Compute the answer after freezing the solver packet.** Independent trusted code reads exactly the files the solver will see and computes **every required key/value**, missingness, precision and tie rule. Treat a model-authored expected JSON or SQL query as a hypothesis. Verify source-native/derived file hashes and row lineage; reject answer-bearing published outputs. Test an independently implemented reference and plausible wrong-method/incomplete-key controls. Never execute proposed Python in a credential-bearing worker.
4. **Screen, build and characterize.** Use a blinded model review only as cheap triage, then scientific/rights/privacy/overlap checks. TaskForge builds a full-key deterministic grader; fresh-agent solver runs and Stage 50/60 review determine whether a provisional task survives. Preserve every failed and corrected artifact under a new revision. Zero accepted or training-cleared tasks is the current measured outcome.
5. **Measure yield at the right denominator.** Fix the source projection, model/decoding, prompt template, tool limits, iteration memory and per-bucket stop rule before the next matched test on *new independent eligible source buckets*. Count distinct independently executable programs and later characterized TaskSpecs per bucket, separately by original/adapted/synthetic output kind; include all model/tool calls, rejected proposals and review cost. This six-cell trial exposes the answer/resource-contract bottleneck; it does **not** establish cost per good task or justify a broad wave.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Issue #12232 reports nine Pending image groups and 25 unbound oracle bootstrap packages. The served-image generator reads `CurationCatalog.current()`, while the Atlas loader selects a specific snapshot and load; the checked-in map pointer dates from November 21 and the tag inventory from November 24. I found no tag-inventory generator on `atlas-env-audit`; [#11903](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11903) explicitly leaves Atlas registry jobs outside its main-port scope.

**Relevant code**
- [`image_registry.py#L110-L121`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/00d5202570cdeb7357853cc447b0249a79d15187/experiments/post_training/task_curation/image_registry.py#L110-L121) — chooses the current served snapshot.
- [`image_registry.py#L257-L295`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/00d5202570cdeb7357853cc447b0249a79d15187/experiments/post_training/task_curation/image_registry.py#L257-L295) — publishes the map and revision pointer.
- [`load.py#L815-L827`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/00d5202570cdeb7357853cc447b0249a79d15187/infra/marina/apps/rl_data_catalog/load.py#L815-L827) — selects and returns the loaded snapshot.
- [`check_image_visibility.py#L134-L155`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/00d5202570cdeb7357853cc447b0249a79d15187/experiments/post_training/task_curation/check_image_visibility.py#L134-L155) — reads GHCR package visibility.

# Proposed Fix

1. Add a repeatable tag-inventory generator on the Atlas branch. Join GHCR package/version/tag metadata to frozen TaskSpec image pins, source bindings and census receipts; classify shared, external, infrastructure and unbound images explicitly. Validate the generated row count, digests and unresolved references against the November 24 CSV.
2. Key the served-image map to the Atlas loader's selected `snapshot_id`. After each catalog load, generate the map and tag inventory for that same load, record `load_id` and `snapshot_id` with both artifact revisions, and advance their pointers only after both outputs validate. Cover shared digests, missing packages, snapshot changes and incomplete publication with local fixture tests.
3. Decide each of the nine Pending groups source by source: qualify and serve its frozen image pins, or record retirement. Apply the existing Daytona census and admission gates before serving the over-budget groups; resolve the missing `rl-data-browsecomp-plus` package reference in its own source decision.
4. Trace the 25 bootstrap packages to their build inputs and source declarations. Bind live packages to pinned TaskSpecs or retire them after checking current and historical references. Complete the issue when every Pending group and bootstrap package has a recorded disposition and a catalog load regenerates both artifacts with no unexplained Atlas-relevant tags.

issues.body:
Track biology evaluation coverage, tooling, and results for reference models and Snowball.

[Biology evaluations catalog](https://openathena.ai/bio-evals/) · [Catalog source](https://github.com/Open-Athena/bio-evals)

**Living summary — updated October 22, 2026.** Detailed evidence is linked from each result.

### Current results

| Model / benchmark | Result | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Snowball v0.1 Smartie Step14 / BixBench corrections v3 / Pi 1.3.0 | **19/205 (9.3%)**; all scored, only 48 nonempty submissions | [Result and reviewed trace audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6300963037) |
| Snowball v0.1 / BiomniBench-DA / Pi 0.87.0 / 60-minute protocol | **4.24/100**; 50/50 scored, 12/50 with any nonempty report (5/50 with both) | [EvalDash](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261022-165801-snowball-v01-biomnibench-da-60min-full-b3c4) · [Comparison and audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6349556649) |
| GLM-5.3 / BiomniBench-DA / Pi 0.87.0 / 60-minute protocol | **71.14/100**; 50/50 scored, 45/50 with both reports | [EvalDash](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261022-165801-glm-5.3-biomnibench-da-60min-full-b3c4) · [Comparison and audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6349556649) |
| GLM-5.3 / MMLU biology | **462/554**; 81.79% mean subject accuracy, 83.39% pooled | [Run and subject results](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/glm53-mmlu-biology-full-20260918-191647) (Marina access) |
| GLM-5.3 / BixBench CLI v1.5 / Terminus-2 | **101/187 graded (54.01%)**; 18/205 ungraded | [Baseline and limitations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667) |
| GLM-5.3 / BixBench-Verified-50 / Terminus-2 | **42/49 graded (85.71%)**; 1/50 ungraded; saved-answer regrade | [Regrade and provenance](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180#issuecomment-5766684283) |
| GLM-5.3 / BixBench-Verified-50 / Pi 0.87.0 | **39/46 graded (84.78%)**; 4/50 ungraded | [Run investigation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6086246928) |

Across benchmark rows, variants, agents, judges, budgets, and grading policies differ. The two BiomniBench-DA rows share the task/input preparation, Pi agent, rubric/judge and budget policy, with disclosed model-serving differences and reused early completions. BiomniBench-DA tasks with no nonempty report score zero; these scores are rubric-score means, not accuracy. Other GLM rows separately report ungraded outcomes.

### Current findings

Snowball’s BixBench failures are dominated by **156 missing answer files**, plus one empty submission. Traces show answers left in chat, simulated execution without real tool calls, repetition, and specific analysis mistakes. Compaction count showed little association with missing files. BFCL also had **55/123 missing submissions**; four inspected examples show related submission/tool-use failures beyond biology, without establishing one shared cause. No scores were changed.

The completed BiomniBench-DA comparison scores **Snowball 4.24/100 versus GLM-5.3 71.14/100**, with all 50 outcomes per model verified against native rewards, sealed archives and EvalDash rows. Snowball produced no nonempty report on 38/50 tasks; GLM did so on 5/50. All 38 selected Snowball cases ended normally within 24 minutes, so the separately confirmed Pi timeout leak cannot explain them. This supports a file-delivery/tool-use gap under these model-serving configurations; checkpoint versus tool/serving integration remains unresolved, and this does not establish a general biology knowledge deficit.

The 60-minute protocol retained 83 unaffected outcomes from the earlier 30-minute budget and reran deadline-affected tasks from scratch. It uses five disclosed input variants and a replacement MiniMax judge/signed rubric scorer, remains supplementary, and does not change the release aggregate. The continuation used the [Harbor timeout repair](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/3bc27cbcffad1d92ad5d9bd4c83cd3f36bf89372); an unresolved `/tokenize` HTTP 502 diagnostic affects interpretation of one GLM timeout. [Full comparison, launch-source references, audit and limitations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6349556649).

[Selected HF traces](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples) show recurring simulated execution, chat-only answers, and repetitive output-limit failures across BiomniBench-DA, BixBench, and BFCL. BiomniBench also has wrong-path and rejected-write examples. These support general execution/submission problems without establishing a shared cause; [the comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6297505720) records the examples and differing Pi versions.

comments.body:
🤖 BixBench CLI development check: the explicit 10 GiB retry ran through the agent phase, but produced no scored answer. The initial attempt had been blocked before model inference because the task's default 20 GB disk request exceeded the Daytona account's 10 GB per-sandbox cap.

The retry used `environment.override_storage_mb: 10240`, following a [previous Harbor canary that hit the same limit](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/75#issuecomment-5461786985). Development outcome:

- Sandbox setup completed. The agent ran for its original 3,600-second budget without creating `/workspace/answer.txt`.
- BixBench's unchanged verifier returns without writing a reward when the answer file is missing. Harbor recorded `RewardFileNotFoundError`; no Together judge decision was produced. The canonical record reports **1 attempted, 0 scored**. This is not a judged incorrect answer or a benchmark accuracy estimate.
- The end-of-agent filesystem diagnostic reported **25.7 MiB used and 9.97 GiB available** in the 10 GiB allocation. No disk-exhaustion failure was observed. This is a final filesystem reading, not peak usage or the base image's total size, and it does not establish that every capsule fits.

Protocol:

- CLI adaptation, registry `bixbench-cli@1.5`, [task revision `711ff277`](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-datasets/tree/711ff277ae6b9e3950d19b40bc3e5aeb96e62b73/datasets/bixbench-cli). One development task, `bix-1-q1`, excluded from the subsequent five-question pilot. The complete registry snapshot has 205 questions.
- GLM-5.3 with Terminus-2; Harbor [`7b18505a`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/7b18505a56e5624f55887e3b20f4de452f698a7a) and its dependency lockfile. Use the [September evaluation policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9193): 32,768 input tokens, 8,192 output tokens, and the default enabled summarization.
- Together `openai/gpt-oss-120b` verifier with BixBench's original grading prompt and Boolean response schema. Four basic live checks passed: exact and equivalent numeric answers accepted; wrong and empty answers rejected. This checks grader integration, not broad judge accuracy.
- The original base image is ARM-only. Use the [adapter author's AMD64 replacement](https://github.com/Future-House/BixBench/issues/41#issuecomment-4340332343), pinned to `sha256:485e5c776422fece8cb98addba593ea188c8a97162807a91d2a0e350522407b7`, with capsule data pinned to Hugging Face revision `f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a`.

The five-question pilot has not been launched. Before expanding, review the no-answer timeout behavior and complete a native verifier check that reaches the judge. The current failure remains in the record; it must not disappear from attempted coverage. This exploratory CLI protocol should be reported separately from the original notebook-based BixBench leaderboard and from Marin's canonical benchmark suite.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 The five-question GLM-5.3 BixBench CLI pilot completed with an answer from every task. The original verifier scored three answers: one correct, two incorrect, and two unscored because structured JSON generation exhausted the judge's token limit. The incomplete original run retains no aggregate metric.

A separate, uniform regrade of the same five saved answers added an explicit JSON-schema instruction to the judge. It produced one correct and four incorrect results, with no JSON errors; the three previously valid grades stayed unchanged. This is a five-question integration pilot with a disclosed judge-prompt variation, not a full-benchmark accuracy estimate. The original answers, trajectories, and scores were preserved.

The format repair is in [Harbor commit `97037f79`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800). It preserves the comparison prompt, Boolean schema, judge model, and 1,024-token cap. Lint and formatting passed. The branch has no PR yet; existing registry snapshots still require regenerated or explicitly patched tasks.

Error review:

- `bix-11-q2`: 88/249 fungal trees exceed the treeness threshold, giving 35.34%, versus the reference's 35%. The regrader rejected the difference. This is a likely precision-related false negative; no score has been changed. The pinned question specifies no rounding rule, and its archive contains no reference notebook.
- `bix-52-q2`: the agent used pooled CpGs / genome length. The [reference capsule](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-4dceea58-7d66-4576-bfc6-88c026d5b7a9.zip) groups only chromosomes containing retained CpGs (notebook cells 11 and 39). Averaging those 20 chromosome densities yields 1.1283e-7, inside the reference interval. The notebook confirms the chromosome selection; the mean was recomputed from the saved table.
- `bix-28-q1`: the final analysis substituted raw terminal branch lengths and species-level medians for the [PhyKIT long-branch statistic](https://jlsteenwyk.com/PhyKIT/reference/commands/long_branch_score.html). The reference p-value has not been independently reproduced; its archive also contains no reference notebook.
- `bix-6-q7`: the agent used a top-1% replicate intersection, then mistook its own intermediate enrichment CSV for supplied results. The [reference notebook](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-f4dcda89-678d-403d-b155-1483d0071765.zip), cells 28–30, instead takes the minimum replicate P-value, selects values below 0.05, maps RefSeq IDs to symbols, and runs Reactome enrichment against measured genes. It reports “cGMP effects” with raw P ≈ 0.000024 and adjusted P ≈ 0.0327. These are saved reference outputs, not a fresh rerun.
- `bix-18-q2`: the mean swarming area was correctly rounded to 82,000.

Six additional fixed judge diagnostics accepted `35.0%` as equivalent to `35%`, rejected `45%`, and classified one value inside and one outside the CpG reference interval correctly. The exact-percent and higher-precision examples returned provider server errors, so this check did not resolve the rounding concern. No tolerance or solver setting was retuned.

The [previously documented protocol](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5736346928) and explicit environment overrides were retained. All five pilot agents submitted within their original time limits, with no observed disk exhaustion. The full 205-question run remains pending a decision on numerical grading; original scores will remain intact.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 GLM-5.3 completed 205 fresh BixBench CLI attempts: **101 correct / 187 graded (54.01%)**, with **18 ungraded**. Grading coverage is **91.22%**. Marin's 95% interval accounting for ungraded items is **43.79–63.43%**; 54.01% is the accuracy among graded questions.

All 177 valid native grades were retained. Eleven saved answers whose verifier calls failed with HTTP 503 received one additional grading attempt each, with the original SDK retry policy. Ten obtained grades (eight correct, two incorrect); one still failed with a provider error. No solver was rerun or answer edited. The original run and its artifacts remain preserved.

The 18 ungraded outcomes are:

- 14 missing answer/reward files following the 3,600-second agent limit.
- Two sandbox processes killed with exit 137 (`TmuxBatchProtocolError`); the cause is unconfirmed.
- One Daytona HTTP 502 gateway failure.
- One unresolved judge server error (`bix-10-q2`).

Three other trials reported `AgentTimeoutError` but produced valid verifier results; those grades remain included. Missing grades are excluded from the accuracy denominator and shown separately. The original private exporter mistakenly required 100% grading coverage; its incomplete record is preserved. The derived result applies [Marin's standard 90% completion gate](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a28c29a008a3ddc1a62fb348c52217a4429e5491/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py), consistent with the reporting policy in #9193. The original sample export displayed missing rewards as incorrect; the derived archive preserves all 18 as ungraded.

Protocol: `bixbench-cli@1.5`, Harbor `7b18505a56e5624f55887e3b20f4de452f698a7a`, task revision `711ff277ae6b9e3950d19b40bc3e5aeb96e62b73`, Terminus-2, 16 concurrent trials, 32,768 input / 8,192 output tokens, default summarization, and 3,600-second agent / 600-second verifier limits. The judge was Together `openai/gpt-oss-120b` with the original comparison prompt and 1,024-token cap. The [explicit JSON-schema repair](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800) applied to every task; numerical tolerances were unchanged. The [previously documented](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5742640265) 10 GiB disk override, pinned AMD64 image, and task-manifest hash were retained.

Validation checked all 205 task identities, sample counts against aggregate scores, all retained native grades, and the eleven selected recovery cases. Two archived trajectories were also compared byte-for-byte through the dashboard API. This establishes an exploratory CLI baseline; ID/OOD status remains unassigned. The replacement judge, missing grades, known precision caveat from the pilot, and unavailable exact serving weights revision limit comparisons with other protocols. Next: review full-run scientific errors and compare future models under this same recorded protocol.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 Reviewed all 86 recorded incorrect answers and all 18 ungraded outcomes from the [completed BixBench CLI baseline](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667), using saved answers/trajectories and the archived reference notebooks where available. No solver or judge calls were rerun. The result remains **101/187 correct (54.01%), with 18/205 ungraded**.

Each incorrect answer has a primary review category:

| Category | Questions | Interpretation |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Observed analysis or protocol divergence | 54 | Identified differences in statistic, counting unit, filtering, cohort, model or enrichment workflow. Some choices are underspecified in the question; these are not all established scientific mistakes. |
| Answer precision or representation review | 11 | Submitted values may differ through rounding or units; this does not establish 11 false negatives. |
| Question or reference adjudication | 7 | Contradictory targets, unclear counting/aggregation, or unresolved reference-data provenance. |
| Numerical or pipeline mismatch unresolved | 14 | Insufficient evidence to isolate the cause without reconstructing more of the reference pipeline. |

The review ledger records a finding, confidence level, trace evidence and pinned reference capsule for each of the 104 nonpassing outcomes. Original trajectories remain in the existing evaluation archive; the detailed review ledger is retained with the private evaluation handoff. The categories above are follow-up queues, not a corrected accuracy estimate.

Concrete analysis findings:

- `bix-61-q1`: reported **4,818 discarded read pairs across two samples**. The MDR trimming log reconstructs the reference's **344,895 discarded individual reads** exactly: 334,988 forward-only survivors + 1,075 reverse-only survivors + 2 × 4,416 fully dropped pairs. Both the counting unit and sample scope changed.
- `bix-28-q4` and `bix-45-q5`: substituted a different statistic. The former used terminal-branch means grouped by species instead of per-tree long-branch scores; the latter used BUSCO score/cutoff instead of [PhyKIT relative composition variability](https://jlsteenwyk.com/PhyKIT/tutorials/pages/01-summarizing-information-content.html).
- `bix-16-q1/q3`: raw Chronos scores were used without the reference's sign reversal. `bix-20-q1/q3`: unclassified variants entered the denominator; the reference excludes them, giving 13/14 and 35/37. These differences are visible in the [essentiality reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-bda54b38-9b49-4009-aad6-d5f52675438a.zip), cell 34, and [variant reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-2ccdbe37-0a92-47b5-9bab-fa8a8c470799.zip), cell 18.
- RNA-seq failures repeatedly differed in count normalization, outlier exclusion, covariates, nominal versus adjusted p-values, enrichment gene lists and background. For example, the [JBX13 reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-1d54e4a7-8b0f-4224-bd31-efcfded0d46c.zip) removes three samples and models replicate, strain and medium; several answers retained all samples and omitted replicate. The [UBE2M reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-308d53bf-1513-4a09-913b-3a1112f94e7b.zip) removes KL3/WL3 before enrichment, unlike the `bix-53-q6` answer. Exact contributions were not isolated through reruns.
- `bix-10` / `bix-29` severity questions also expose a reference-definition caveat: the [reference preprocessing](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-fbe0e950-76f2-4eb7-a216-a2d377970922.zip), cell 17, aggregates all adverse events per participant, although questions call the endpoint COVID severity. COVID-specific/event-level alternatives therefore need protocol adjudication.

Grading and reference findings:

- `bix-19-q2` is a calculation-versus-submission example: the agent computed **Cohen's d = 0.216284**, independently matching [reference cell 30](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-8c64b1fa-fdcc-41e2-be8d-2f0c8d5faaa1.zip), but submitted approximately **0.22**. That final answer falls outside the target interval **0.215–0.217**. Other precision candidates include 35.34% versus 35% and 5.23 versus 5.2. The 11 cases are `4-q1/q5/q6`, `11-q1/q2/q5`, `19-q2`, `28-q6`, `38-q1/q3`, and `54-q5`, all with prefix `bix-`. Tiny nonzero p-values are not automatically equivalent to literal zero; `54-q5` also has a model-input difference alongside its ratio/fraction representation.
- `bix-53-q4` has a confirmed malformed target: the question requests a **pathway count**, but the [original ideal answer](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/BixBench.jsonl) is **4.25E-04**. [Reference cell 79](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-308d53bf-1513-4a09-913b-3a1112f94e7b.zip) explicitly counts **2** pathways. The submitted answer was **1**, so fixing the target would not automatically make it correct.
- `bix-31-q2` contradicts its stated analysis. The target interval **−0.45 to −0.35** conflicts with **abs(LFC)>0.5**. [Reference cells 32–38](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-b1dbace7-f6e9-42ec-81e1-bcc24161cc27.zip) show FAM138A at baseMean **0.483698**, unshrunk LFC **−0.383938**, and shrunk LFC **−0.060666**. The target matches the unshrunk, low-expression row despite instructions requiring shrinkage and baseMean>10. The agent answered `NA`.
- `bix-52-q1` has a reference-data bug: [reference cell 14](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-4dceea58-7d66-4576-bfc6-88c026d5b7a9.zip) downloads **JD_Chromosome_Length.csv** into **ZF_Chromosome_Length.csv**. The agent's **1.52** ratio is internally consistent with the supplied lengths and site counts; the provenance of the target **0.47–0.67** remains unresolved. `bix-52-q5` also counts repeated records instead of distinct sites, so this data caveat does not explain all CpG failures.
- The remaining four primary adjudication cases are `bix-8-q6` (260 unique genes versus 680 transcript records; [reference cell 21](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-48a6b469-9c9d-4bef-b5b4-f29b7d6fa046.zip) counts rows), `bix-38-q6` (median of paired ratios versus ratio of group medians), `bix-43-q4` (8/514 DE genes versus 8/49 pathway genes), and `bix-22-q6` (the origin of the 0.3–0.4 correlation target was not established). These require explicit definitions or reference reconstruction.
- `bix-54-q4` additionally has reversed target interval bounds, but its submitted p-value lies outside even the sorted interval. This metadata defect does not rescue that answer.

The [verifier](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800/adapters/bixbench/src/bixbench/task-template/tests/llm_judge.py) asks an LLM for binary equivalence. It has **no separate global numerical-tolerance rule**; some targets contain explicit intervals. The JSON-schema repair changes response format, not this comparison prompt. Before any rescoring, define a consistent precision/adjudication policy and preserve the present native grades as a separate baseline.

The 14 missing-answer traces show long model fits, repeated workbook inspection, unresolved analysis choices, and sensitivity checks after intermediate results existed. More time alone is not a demonstrated fix. The two exit-137 cases show killed statistical processes; excessive worker creation is a plausible contributor, but an OOM cause is unconfirmed. One gateway failure and `bix-10-q2`'s persistent judge 503 remain ungraded. The latter has a saved answer outside its target interval, but no manual grade was substituted.

Next: adjudicate the flagged question/reference and precision cases; document the intended analysis protocols; then select a small set of failures for any separately approved controlled rerun. Keep any revised scoring or solver results separate from this baseline. The existing verifier JSON-format PR follow-up remains open.

Reference links above use dataset revision `f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a`; notebook cell indices are zero-based. Several phylogenetic and genomic-pipeline capsules contain no reference notebook, which limits causal conclusions for the 14 unresolved cases.

🤖 Agent-runtime summary for the [completed 205-question BixBench CLI run](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667). Measured from each original Harbor trial’s `agent_execution.started_at` and `finished_at`; all 205 have both timestamps.

The median agent runtime was **5.6 minutes per question**. The middle 50% took **1.7–15.5 minutes**, and the 90th percentile was **37.3 minutes**.

| Questions | n | Median, min | 25th–75th percentile, min | 90th percentile, min | Mean, min |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| All attempted questions | 205 | 5.6 | 1.7–15.5 | 37.3 | 12.8 |
| Solver completed without interruption | 185 | 4.7 | 1.6–13.8 | 20.5 | 8.6 |
| Final grade: correct | 101 | 2.3 | 0.9–9.2 | 17.3 | 6.9 |
| Final grade: incorrect | 86 | 8.1 | 2.8–14.8 | 26.5 | 12.3 |

These are elapsed solving times, including model responses, command execution, waits and tool/network latency during the agent phase. They exclude separately timed sandbox setup, agent setup and grading. Quantiles use linear interpolation at `(n−1)×p`.

**17/205 tasks (8.3%) reached the configured 3,600-second agent cap**: 14 had no submitted answer and remained ungraded; 3 retained gradeable answers. The other three interrupted agents had two process-kill failures and one gateway failure. Capped times measure time spent before termination, not the uncensored time required to solve those tasks. Recorded capped durations were 3,600.0–3,602.3 seconds.

The median complete trial duration, including setup, grading and teardown, was **7.3 minutes**. The interval from the first trial start to the last trial finish was **3 h 28 min 48 s**.

The 185 uninterrupted solver completions include one answer whose judge still failed. Correct/incorrect rows use final saved-answer recovery grades and retain the three scored timeouts. Runtime differences between outcome groups are descriptive; task difficulty and workflow differences confound interpretation.

The complete launcher-to-export span was **3 h 36 min 11 s**, with a cap of **16 concurrent trials**. That batch span includes setup and final export; later saved-answer judge recovery is excluded. The [existing result](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667) remains 101/187 correct with 18 ungraded.

Per-question times, raw timestamps, source hashes and the summary calculation are retained in the private evaluation handoff. No new evaluation or grading calls were made.

Eight cases are equivalent when rounded to the reference's displayed precision, but that is a review criterion, not an adopted universal scoring rule. Zero-valued p-value targets require an explicit threshold or precision rule. A defective task does not automatically make its submitted answer correct.

Submitted Mann–Whitney p = 2.0944e-26; saved two-sided asymptotic calculation gives U = 3556 and p = 2.0944031684e-26. The ideal 0.0 contains no usable significance threshold or numerical tolerance. No original reference notebook was available for this capsule. | Ask for a nonzero reference p-value with documented test options, or an explicit threshold/rounding instruction. Do not infer that every small p-value is equivalent to zero. |
| [bix-19-q2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-8c64b1fa-fdcc-41e2-be8d-2f0c8d5faaa1.zip) | Cohen's d ≈ 0.22 (KD − CTRL mean difference = 3.875 NeuN; pooled SD) → Between 0.215 and 0.217 inclusive | **Submitted-answer precision error**. Both the saved calculation and notebook give Cohen's d = 0.2162844172. Do not replace a submitted answer with a better number from the trajectory. Future instructions should state the required precision. |
| [bix-22-q6](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-34a4ea96-c800-4c11-959e-57cdc4932c52.zip) | 0.0504 → Between 0.3 and 0.4 inclusive | **Unresolved analysis specification**. None supports target 0.3–0.4. | Specify sample set, gene filter, expression summary and whether correlation is pooled or cell-type specific; regenerate the reference from that pipeline. A factor-of-ten typo is plausible but not established, and the agent and notebook use different cohorts. |
| [bix-28-q6](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-c66d3ed9-0a95-46be-a237-ed68498ea7f6.zip) | 5.23 → 5.2 | **Presentation-equivalent candidate**. 5.23 rounds to 5.2; saved calculation is 5.2282463. | Accept only in a separately versioned policy allowing equivalence at the displayed reference precision; do not change the native grade. |
| [bix-31-q2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-b1dbace7-f6e9-42ec-81e1-bcc24161cc27.zip) | NA → Between -0.45 and -0.35 inclusive | **Confirmed task/reference defect**. The capsule annotation identifies FAM138A as lncRNA. Notebook cell 26 fits batch + sex; cell 32 gives baseMean 0.483698 and unshrunk LFC -0.383938; cell 36 gives shrunk LFC -0.060666. The target -0.45 to -0.35 matches the unshrunk row, contradicting the protein-coding, baseMean >10, abs(LFC)>0.5 and shrinkage requirements. NA is defensible for exclusion. | Minimal repair: explicitly ask for the unshrunk FAM138A sex coefficient from the batch + sex model before those filters. | [bix-38-q1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-975f3e91-53b0-44b1-ac9f-20023d9c8cd0.zip) | 2.18-fold (fungi / animals) → 2x larger in fungi | **Presentation-equivalent candidate**. 2.18-fold agrees with the coarse 2x target. Recomputed ratio of full-precision group medians is 2.177433; ratio of rounded IQ-TREE report medians is 2.177509. | Accept only in a separately versioned policy allowing equivalence at the displayed reference precision; do not change the native grade. |

Independent Newick branch-length sums find 96 paired orthologs and median(fungal_length/animal_length) = 1.9036165971, matching the submission. The target 2.178 instead matches the ratio of separately rounded group medians, 3.0962/1.4219 = 2.1775089669; that uses all 249 fungal and 100 animal trees. Full-precision group medians give 2.177433, also a different estimand. | Keep the paired-ratio question; reference 1.9036165971 with a declared tolerance, or explicitly request 1.904 to three decimal places. Preserve the paired ortholog list and full-precision input calculation. |
| [bix-43-q4](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-15ff11e5-2db1-45b6-b3a3-46bc2a74b821.zip) | 8/514 → 8/49 | **Unresolved analysis specification**. The prompt asks for the proportion of differentially expressed genes, but reference cell 65 reports the Enrichr overlap 8/49, whose denominator is pathway members. Agent 8/514 uses its DEG denominator. The notebook has 679 pre-mapping DEG rows at cell 45 and drops missing gene names at cell 53; the final distinct mapped denominator was not established. | Minimal repair: ask for the Enrichr Overlap field, explicitly defined as intersecting genes / pathway genes, and retain 8/49. If retaining the DEG-proportion wording, establish mapping/deduplication and recompute that denominator. Do not certify 514 as the reference count. |
| [bix-52-q1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-4dceea58-7d66-4576-bfc6-88c026d5b7a9.zip) | Chromosome W / chromosome 1 = 1.52 → Between 0.47 and 0.67 inclusive | **Confirmed task/reference defect**. Packaged ZF_Chromosome_Length.csv is byte-identical to JD_Chromosome_Length.csv (SHA256 59e321ef…051b); notebook cell 14 downloads the JD file under the ZF name. Three W and 29 chr1 distinct filtered sites give 1.519930 with that supplied table. The original Zenodo ZF table gives W length 20,846,394 and chr1 length 114,020,016, yielding 0.56581364, inside the existing 0.47–0.67 interval. | Replace the mislabeled capsule asset and notebook download URL with the original ZF table (Zenodo record 12205202, MD5 b078a4dab5b677bfd0742452de6b1a17). | [bix-53-q4](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-308d53bf-1513-4a09-913b-3a1112f94e7b.zip) | 1 → 4.25E-04 | **Confirmed task/reference defect**. The original dataset ideal is 4.25E-04 for a question asking how many pathways. Notebook cell 79 explicitly counts two oxidative terms among the top twenty. The submitted one is not correct merely because the gold is malformed. | Use integer target 2 only with the notebook's intended cohort, adjusted-p filtering, shrinkage and pathway-term matching explicitly specified. The current question says p while the notebook filters padj; pin that distinction before a corrected task is released. |
| [bix-54-q5](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-9e52daf6-ca58-43e8-e732-fbac3459d295.zip) | 10:1 → Between 0.9 and 0.99 inclusive | **Presentation-equivalent candidate**. 10:1 converts to a component fraction 10/11 = 0.90909, inside 0.90–0.99. Reference cells 16/19 use rhlI/(rhlI+lasI) and yield a spline maximum at 0.9076577. The prompt asks for a ratio but the target stores a fraction. The agent selected the best tested ratio from 36 mixed-culture rows; the reference spline used 39 rows, so final-answer equivalence does not validate the method. | State that the answer is the rhlI fraction; allow an explicitly labeled equivalent mixture ratio if retaining outcome-only grading. Keep the method caveat separate. |

Evidence uses the pinned BixBench dataset `f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a`; task links above point to the corresponding source capsule. Notebook cell numbers are zero-based. Local reproduction records include the downloaded-member SHA256 manifest, gene/correlation checks, and all 96 paired tree ratios. The corrected Zebra Finch file is available in [the original Zenodo dataset](https://zenodo.org/records/12205202).

A separate [public BixBench audit](https://github.com/Anqi-Dai/BixBench_eval/blob/6070dc293677b0ef21fa38d7ab23c5850d8799c0/env/REVIEW_REPORT.md) independently documents the 680-record/260-gene mismatch. Its study covers three capsules and fourteen questions; it does not validate this entire run.

The proposed precision rule was also screened against **all 205 saved outcomes, including the 101 previously correct answers**. This was a conservative scalar/range screen, not a complete semantic regrade: 81 answers require semantic parsing, and counts, unit conversions, reversed ranges and the zero p-value need explicit treatment. It flags two existing passes that a naive comparator would reject: `bix-18-q5` supplies 0.29 against a percent-scale 25–30 target, and `bix-45-q1` supplies 7.70e-54 against 7.6968e-54. The latter needs symmetric handling of reported precision, rather than always requiring the target's extra digits. These findings block adopting a blanket rounding rule or publishing a selectively corrected accuracy.

Harbor Index provides relevant prior work: its public index includes five BixBench-derived tasks, with eighteen trials each. [Its Jackdaw notes](https://hub.harborframework.com/tasks/harbor-index/bix-cpg-density-jackdaw/latest) explicitly say the scientific derivation was not re-audited. Later [PR #142](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-index/pull/142) fixed underspecified instructions for two tasks present in this run: miRNA analysis `bix-30-q1` ([issue #97](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-index/issues/97)) and ordinal regression `bix-10-q2` ([issue #113](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-index/issues/113)). The fixes specify preprocessing/modeling choices while retaining the targets. These are useful precedents for task repair, not grounds for changing our recorded grades. The index uses its own 1,200-second budgets and deterministic numeric verifiers; its results are not directly comparable to this baseline.

Next: review the seven local upstream-report drafts; agree on versioned task repairs and numerical tolerances; then validate any revised grader across all 205 outcomes before publishing a separate result. The fourteen other numerical/pipeline discrepancies and ungraded outcomes remain follow-ups. The main issue table records **per-question agent time**, with no total-duration column.
